user.title: Choose a base map
user.description:
This integration replaces the base map of Home Assistant's built-in map with a Chinese map provider.

Tiles are fetched by the Home Assistant server, and the China datum shift is applied there too, so the app and web UI show identical maps and no API key is ever sent to the browser. Only Tianditu needs an API key (free of charge, choose the "browser" application type).

data_description.map_source: AMap / Tencent / Baidu need no key. The vector, image and terrain Tianditu layers share one key.
data_description.api_key: Key of the currently selected source. Stored on the Home Assistant server only.

abort.single_instance_allowed: The base map is a global setting, so only one instance is allowed. Change it in the existing entry's options.

error.key_required: The selected map source requires an API key.
error.invalid_key: The API key is invalid or expired.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the validation server. Check the network of your Home Assistant host.

init.title: China Maps settings
init.description: Pick a map source, enter its key and tune the offset fix. You can also switch sources from the toolbar in the bottom-right corner of the map.

data_description.map_source: Switching the source keeps the keys you already entered.
data_description.api_key: Key of the currently selected source; leave empty when the source needs none.
data_description.fix_china_offset: Chinese map services use GCJ-02 / BD-09 while Home Assistant entities are WGS84. With the fix enabled the tiles are shifted back so roads and entities line up (default on).
data_description.precise_offset: On: up to 4 upstream tiles are stitched per tile (most accurate). Off: a single tile is fetched (cheaper, accuracy drops to one tile, about ±300 m at z18).

error.key_required: The selected map source requires an API key.
error.invalid_key: The API key is invalid or expired.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the validation server. Check the network of your Home Assistant host.
